govt_response.summary: At launch roughly half the seats on each flight were to cost Rs 2,500 for a one-hour flight; a later explainer reports over 580 routes operationalised across 85+ airports/heliports/water aerodromes by April 2026 (secondary source, not verified). No ministry rebuttal of the CAG report was located.

analysis:
Modi launched UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) at Shimla on 27 April 2017, saying his aim was for ordinary people wearing 'hawai chappal' to travel by air; the scheme capped fares at about Rs 2,500 for 50% of seats on one-hour flights.

The CAG's 2023 audit of rounds 1-3 found that 403 of 774 awarded routes never started, that 371 routes started, 112 completed the three-year concession and 54 were still operating beyond it in March 2023. It also found RCS passenger numbers rose from 2.63 lakh in 2017-18 to 24.97 lakh in 2022-23 and made 16 recommendations.

The claim is an aspiration with no numeric target or deadline, so the verdict reflects the gap between awarded and sustained routes rather than a missed date.
notes: Aspirational statement with no deadline; verdict 'misleading' is a judgement call (alternatives: in-progress/unverifiable).
